commit.description: Bump version, commit all changes, and push to GitHub
commit.template:
Bump the version by incrementing the MINOR number (MAJOR.MINOR format), create a git tag, stage all changes, commit, push to origin master, AND add a new entry to server/changelog.json with the version, today's date, and the commit description. Steps:
1. Get the LATEST tag: git tag --sort=-version:refname | Select-Object -First 1
2. Parse vMAJOR.MINOR (e.g., v1.22), increment MINOR, form new tag (e.g., v1.23)
3. Read server/changelog.json, prepend a new entry: {"version": "vX.YY", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "description": "<USER_MESSAGE>"}, write it back
4. Stage all: git add -A
5. Commit: git commit -m "<USER_MESSAGE>"
6. Create the new tag on the new commit: git tag <NEW_VERSION>
7. Push: git push origin master
8. Push tags: git push origin --tags
IMPORTANT: use PowerShell for all git commands. Create the tag AFTER the commit, not before. Add the changelog entry BEFORE staging. The user will provide the commit message in the same message. Execute all steps and report the new version.
